title: Procreate Sketchbook — Illustrator's Process Diary
description: A Procreate-inspired slide built on iPad watercolor paper texture, with loose graphite construction lines peeking beneath soft peach watercolor washes that bleed at their edges — sealed with a script caption and an inked date stamp in the corner.
philosophy: This template exists for illustrators who believe the process is as worthy of display as the finished piece. It refuses polish: the pencil under-drawing stays visible, the watercolor blooms imperfectly, and the handwriting wobbles — because authenticity is the entire point. It is designed for intimate, first-person storytelling in sketchbook form, not for persuading a room or selling a product. Its audience leans in close rather than sitting back.
goodFor: Illustrator WIP and process walkthrough posts
Art school or workshop portfolio presentations
avoidFor: Product launch or promotional campaign slides
Dense academic citation or footnote-heavy layouts
author: harness

examples.promptCore: A sketchbook cover that feels lifted from a working illustrator's bag — soft watercolor wash pools in the upper-right and bleeds unevenly toward the edge as though still damp, while loose graphite construction lines ghost beneath it, implying structure without announcing it. The mood is intimate and unhurried, like a diary page held up to diffused afternoon light. Composition is asymmetric and slightly weighted left, with generous empty paper breathing around the title area. Avoid anything centered, symmetrical, or suggestive of digital production polish.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed watercolor paper texture as base; title block anchored in the lower-left quadrant spanning roughly 60% of the horizontal field, leaving the upper-right open for the watercolor bloom element. A ghost graphite construction grid underlays the entire surface — present but visually subordinate to the wash layer. Script subtitle sits one irregular line-height beneath the title, left-aligned with no rule separation. Inked date stamp occupies the bottom-right corner; no top header band, no enclosing frame.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a torn page from a working sketchbook — intimate and unresolved, where an in-progress sketch or wash study is the undisputed hero and words exist only as marginal notes scrawled in haste alongside it. Compositional rhythm is asymmetric and quietly breathing: one generous visual zone commands attention while small annotative text fragments drift at slight angles in the remaining space. Avoid any suggestion of presentation polish, rigid alignment, or visual completion — the entire appeal lives in visible process, paper grain, watercolor bloom, and the honest wobble of a hand that draws because it must, not because it performs.

examples.layoutNotes: Loose 12-col grid with a dominant sketch or watercolor wash panel occupying roughly two-thirds of the canvas (cols 1–8, bleeding to the left and top edges). The remaining third carries staggered handwritten annotation blocks at varying heights — not a bulleted list, but offset caption lines that drift slightly off the baseline. A small inked date stamp or folio mark sits anchored to the lower-right corner outside the main content field. A ghost construction-line underlay bleeds through the wash panel as a visible secondary layer beneath the primary content element.
